subject: AWS listing verbiage check — buyer path alignment
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Horowitz <alex@cloudfleet.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: AWS listing verbiage check — buyer path alignment

Alex — attaching the latest draft for the AWS Marketplace entry and a lightweight pricing CSV. We made two deliberate wording choices I want to highlight before we lock the page: 

1) Buyer path headline: we swapped "Deploy in minutes" for "Deploy with predictable throughput" to emphasize Dedicated capacity and set expectations on performance and cost.
2) Metering blurb: we reduced the technical detail in favor of a short footprint example for common ML workloads (see pricing_table_sheet.csv).

Can you confirm that (a) the emphasis on throughput vs. speed aligns with CloudFleet's procurement/ops messaging, and (b) your procurement team is comfortable with the proposed metering footnote?

Attachments: aws_listing_draft_v3.docx, pricing_table_sheet.csv

Quick asks: 
- Alex: redline any phrasing that misrepresents your managed instance SLA or trial entitlements.
- Kimberly/Aditya: can you sanity-check the buyer-path CTA flows (trial -> privateoffer -> Dedicated)?

Thanks — I kept the copy tight to reduce legal churn but added two optional callouts (Performance Guarantees, Network Controls) later in the doc if you want to expand.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Horowitz <alex@cloudfleet.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudFleet Procurement <procurement@cloudfleet.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS listing verbiage check — buyer path alignment

Thanks Mina — this is helpful. A few notes after a quick pass: 

- Headline swap: We like the move to "predictable throughput" but suggest adding a short parenthetical to not lose newer buyers: "(fast startup for small jobs)" — otherwise some of our SME buyers may assume slow cold-starts.
- Metering footnote: Procurement flagged the example in pricing_table_sheet.csv as optimistic for bursty GPU workloads. They asked if we can add a short sentence: "Actual metering may vary during burst; contact sales for commit-backed pricing."
- Trial entitlements: Procurement confirms a 14-day trial is fine but wants an explicit note about max concurrent sessions during trial (they require a cap for POC fairness).

I've forwarded to procurement for wording suggestions; see inline comments in the attached DocX (I added two tracked comments).

On the whole this is close — only a couple of risk points on expectations. If you prefer, I can join a 20-min sync early next week to sign off.

— Alex Horowitz
Product Lead, Integrations
CloudFleet Inc.
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Horowitz <alex@cloudfleet.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS listing verbiage check — buyer path alignment

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick read and the tracked comments. 

Planned updates I'm taking on before your procurement's final pass: 
- Add the parenthetical to the headline: "Deploy with predictable throughput (fast startup for small jobs)."
- Insert the metering clarification sentence into the pricing footnote.
- Add a one-line POC limitation under Trial entitlements: "Trials permit up to 3 concurrent sessions per account." (let me know if procurement wants a different cap).

Kimberly/Aditya — FYI I'm updating the doc now. If you see any downstream UX implications in the Console messaging (trial CTA -> privateoffer flow), call them out in the Drive link.

I'll upload aws_listing_draft_v4.docx and ping when done. If Alex is available a quick 20-min sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT would let us close the remaining language and expedite procurement sign-off.

— Mina
From: CloudFleet Procurement <procurement@cloudfleet.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Alex Horowitz <alex@cloudfleet.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 08:30 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick read and the tracked comments.
> 
> Planned updates I'm taking on before your procurement's final pass:
> - Add the parenthetical to the headline: "Deploy with predictable throughput (fast startup for small jobs)."
> - Insert the metering clarification sentence into the pricing footnote.
> - Add a one-line POC limitation under Trial entitlements: "Trials permit up to 3 concurrent sessions per account." (let me know if procurement wants a different cap).

Thanks Mina — procurement team reviewed the suggested cap and requests the following minor edits before final approval: 

- POC cap: please change to "up to 2 concurrent sessions per trial account" — this reduces shared resource risk during trials.
- Evidence: procurement asked for a link to your SOC2 evidence summary (we need a one-page pointer in the listing or as a footnote).

If you can confirm both items in the aws_listing_draft_v4 upload today we can issue a procurement green-light and proceed with the PrivateOffer term sheet.

Procurement (on behalf of CloudFleet Inc.)
